newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes up on weather, exports and funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes up on weather, exports and funds.

text.p: Cold weather and a hike in export workings combined with fund short covering to boost CBOT corn futures to a higher close, traders said.
"Corn hung in there on weather and there's a little business around," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

The cold weather will increase feed consumption of the nation's livestock. But many traders said funds were short corn and were getting out of those positions before the expiration of the December contract at 1201 CST Thursday. Funds were short corn roughly 210 million bushels entering Tuesday's session, the traders said.
"People are getting out of the December shorts, said Paul Haugens, vice president for FIMAT Futures. Also "there may be a little corn/bean and corn/wheat spreading," he said.
Corn has lagged the gains in wheat and soybeans and the spread was due to correct before expiration day, they said.
"Corn has been weak and there is fund short covering today. Plus there have been no deliveries and virtually no farmer selling," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Corn closed 3/4 to two cents per bushel higher, with December up 3/4 at $2.70-3/4 a bushel.

Traders said the corn market also found support early this week on a little brighter outlook for U.S. exports. Monday's USDA weekly export inspections report showed the weekly tally above expectations.

Also USDA early Monday announced a sale of 105,000 tonnes of corn to unknown destinations and matched that with an announcement early Tuesday of another sale of 105,000 tonnes to unknown destinations.
But "business is still pretty limited. There is a little business around but nothing big and Japan is quiet," Haugens said. "There are still rumors China has corn for sale which I think is possible."

Traders said funds bought at least 15.0 million bushels of corn Tuesday with Griffin Trading and Rosenthal Collins each purchasing four million bushels of March and SAK Futures bought five million bushels of March, traders said.
Futures volume was estimated at 55,000 contracts, above the 47,988 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Smith Barney bought 700 May $3.00 calls at 2-1/2 to 2-3/4 cents, Rand Financial bought 500 May $3.00 calls and sold 500 May $2.70 puts at 9-1/2 to 10 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, slightly above the 10,792 traded Monday.
